The active-set solver matches brute-force support enumeration, and the controller matches binary search. Note the brute-force comparison used tolerance 1e-7 for x — but the brute-force picks the min-f KKT point; since the problem is strictly convex, the optimum is unique ✓.

Wait — one caveat: the brute worker enumerates supports and picks min f among KKT-consistent points; but for degenerate problems (multiple KKT representations of the same primal), x is unique ✓.

Also I should cross-check with LARGER slot counts and degenerate cases (e.g., identical columns — symmetric paths). Let me add: columns with duplicates possible (two slots same edges) — allowed since different commodities may use identical paths, and within a commodity paths must be distinct... but H could still have identical columns across commodities. The random col generation may already produce identical columns sometimes.

Also test with rho and B extreme to create boundary solutions where x=0 for some slots (force degenerate supports). The random uniform B in [-3,3] with positive demands... route always has x>0 sum = d. In admit, many x=0 cases — covered.
